sexnote.q: Normal hematocrit levels will vary, depending on your sex, age, whether or not you smoke, and the altitude where you live.
sexnote.note: The test is the same for everyone — but the range considered normal is not.

badgedef.base: This test is a component of a routine annual panel (CBC, CMP or lipid panel), so a standard yearly draw would normally already include it.
badgedef.spec: Specialist-ordered rather than routine screening — usually requested to follow up a specific finding, not as a general check.
badgedef.quoted: The description is quoted word-for-word from a named source (MedlinePlus, NCBI or the National Cancer Institute).
badgedef.gen: The description was generated by an AI model from the test's official LOINC name and category. It is NOT quoted from a medical source — follow the LOINC link to verify.
badgedef.score: Relevance score: how strongly this test's stated purpose matches the answers you selected. Higher means a closer keyword match, not a stronger clinical indication.

tests.qs: MedlinePlus (NIH)

tests.n: Bilirubin

tests.n: Hepatitis C antibody
tests.q: "For hepatitis C ... a test can't tell the difference between an active infection and a past infection that has cleared up."
tests.qs: MedlinePlus (NIH)

tests.n: HIV screening (antibody/antigen)
tests.q: "An HIV screening test is used to find out if you have been infected with HIV."
tests.qs: MedlinePlus (NIH)
tests.w: CDC recommends "everyone between the ages of 13 and 64 get tested for HIV at least once as part of routine health care."

tests.n: Procalcitonin
tests.q: "A procalcitonin test is mostly used if you are seriously ill and your provider thinks you may have a systemic infection (an infection that affects your entire body)."
tests.qs: MedlinePlus (NIH)

tests.n: Syphilis tests (RPR / VDRL)
tests.q: "All syphilis tests are used to check your blood for signs of a syphilis infection."
tests.qs: MedlinePlus (NIH)
tests.w: The cited source does not restrict this test to a specific age, sex, region, or race; it is ordered for the general population when clinically indicated.

tests.w: Breast cancer patients

tests.n: Cancer antigen 19-9

tests.qs: MedlinePlus (NIH)

tests.n: Carcinoembryonic antigen

tests.n: Human chorionic gonadotropin

tests.qs: MedlinePlus Encyclopedia (NIH)
tests.w: Primarily pregnant women

tests.n: Prostate-specific antigen
tests.q: "A PSA test is used to screen for prostate cancer."
tests.qs: MedlinePlus (NIH)
tests.w: Males; "Prostate cancer is more common in Black men, who also have a higher risk of developing prostate cancer at a younger age and having more serious disease."
